newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish government commission to probe Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: Swedish government commission to probe Nazi gold.

text.p: The Swedish government plans to set up a commission this week to investigate Nazi gold bought by Sweden during World War Two, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Sunday.
"The purpose is to create as much clarity as possible in this matter," spokesman Hakan Eriksson said.

The decision to form a commission was taken by Foreign Minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen following fresh allegations that Sweden may have disposed of up to seven tonnes of gold bought from Nazi Germany during the war, despite suspicions that some two-thirds of it may have been stolen.

"We will start working this week on appointing members of the commission and setting an agenda for it," Eriksson said. "The commission will keep working until it finds the truth of what happened. We'll see how long it takes."
Sweden's close trade relations with Nazi Germany during the war have come under scrutiny following criticism of Swiss banks' dealings with Hitler's regime.
The World Jewish Congress (WJC), which is seeking to penetrate Swiss bank secrecy, took its search for the unclaimed wealth of Holocaust victims to Sweden last November.

Both countries were neutral during the war but Sweden sold large amounts of iron ore to the Nazis in return for gold that some historians now say may have been looted from Jews or from occupied countries.

Officials said the government commission would replace a recently formed working group made up of representatives from the Foreign Ministry, the central bank, the Swedish Bank Association and the Jewish community in Stockholm.
They said the commission would raise the status of the investigation and was a sign that the government was taking the matter seriously.
The central bank said last week it would launch its own new investigation next month.
The bank last autumn checked whether any of the gold bullion held in Swedish vaults originated from Nazi Germany but no significant connection was found.
The new probe will concentrate on the bank's archives to establish whether any relevant information has been overlooked.
Media reports last week claimed the Swedish wartime government put pressure on the central bank not to ask too many questions about the origins of gold emanating from Nazi Germany.

The daily newspaper Dagens Nyheter and Swedish radio said in a jointly produced report that government complicity was found in memoranda in the central bank archives, written in 1943 and discovered by their reporters.
Sweden returned about 13 tonnes of gold to Belgium and the Netherlands after the war when it was shown it had been looted by occupying Germans.
